text: Microsoft case card dated 2026-08-02. The company is treated as an US-listed stock in this educational case. Its exchange ticker is MSFT. These are frozen classroom facts, not current filings.

Paper-trading policy dated 2026-08-03: only AAPL and MSFT are allowed; max order notional USD 1000; max 5 shares per order and per ticker held; short sales prohibited. Human approval of a proposal is mandatory before the simulated ledger write. Proposals expire after 30 minutes; reject when reference price moves more than 2%.

Data policy dated 2026-08-04: Yahoo Finance via yfinance is unofficial, may be delayed, and may have personal-use restrictions. Reject a market snapshot older than seven calendar days. Do not assert real-time price, guaranteed profits, or recommendations to trade real money.

Technical methodology dated 2026-08-05: SMA20 averages the last 20 daily adjusted closes; SMA50 averages 50; RSI14 uses Wilder-like exponential smoothing; MACD is EMA12 minus EMA26 and signal line EMA9 of MACD. Indicators are descriptive, not price forecasts.

Evaluation protocol dated 2026-08-06: compare no retrieval, fixed top-3 Qdrant retrieval, and agent-chosen Qdrant retrieval on the same 25 frozen questions. Compare two local Ollama models under the same corpus and prompts. Label exact policy facts, check citations and unsupported claims, and repeat three times for consistency. This is an educational QA benchmark, not a backtest or proof of alpha.

Illustrative debate dated 2026-08-07: analyst summarizes evidence and uncertainty; critic challenges stale data, citation gaps, conflicting signals and unsuitable orders. A bounded second analyst pass may correct a critique. No agent can bypass deterministic risk controls or the human approval gate.
